title: Prove the actual-width floors differ on perfect 500th powers
body:
## Summary
- For `d >= 2`, `floor(d^(1/500))` and `floor((d-1)^(1/500))` differ exactly when `d` is a perfect 500th power. This is the matched-layer cut between the old layout and the actual-width plan.
- At `d = 2^500` the floors are 2 and 1. At `2^500 + 1` they agree. The same locus holds for exponent 3 on widths 2 through 299.
- Truncation, layout and host serialization stay unpriced. Partial result. No new kappa and no selected-frontier change.
